decisions.reason: As the flagship of the firm's direction with demand still uncertain after only one year, the option is worth keeping open, and an injection-molded crate costs little to keep in the catalog.
A foldable large container fits core pooling and automotive demand, has its own page, and one year of evidence is too little to resolve its value, so abandoning it would be premature.
Only a mention on the website suggests modest commitment, but a standard stackable crate is cheap to keep in a large portfolio while uncertainty resolves.
The rackable pallet extends an established pallet line at low incremental cost, so keeping it open preserves upside despite the limited visibility so far.
The spill-retention pallet serves a niche regulatory need, has its own page, and costs little to maintain, so the option should stay open.
The pallet with load retainers is a dedicated-page variant addressing beverage and retail handling, and it is too early to conclude its value will not be realized.
